Short title, extent and commencement

NORTH﷓WEST FRONTIER PROVINCE HIGHWAYS AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 2001
NORTH‑WEST
FRONTIER PROVINCE HIGHWAYS AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 2001
ORDINANCE XIX OF 2001
An Ordinance
further to provide for establishment of a Highway Authority to the North‑West
Frontier Province
[Gazette of
N.W.F.P., Extraordinary, 29th August, 2001]
No. Legis: 1‑(15)/71,
dated 29‑8‑2001.‑‑The following Ordinance by the
Governor of the North‑West Frontier Province is hereby published for
general information:‑‑
Whereas it is expedient to
establish, a Highway Authority in the North‑West Frontier Province for
the purposes hereinafter appearing;
And whereas the Governor is
satisfied that circumstances exist which render it necessary to take immediate
action;
Now therefore, in pursuance of
the Proclamation of Emergency of the 14th day of October, 1999, as amended
up-to-date, and the Provisional Constitution Order No.1 of 1999, read with
Article 4 of the Provisional Constitution (Amendment) Order No.9 of 1999, and
in exercise of all powers enabling him in that behalf, the Governor of the
North‑West Frontier Province is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:
CHAPTER ‑ I
PRELIMINARY
1. Short title, extent and
commencement.‑‑(1) This Ordinance may be called the North‑West
Frontier Province Highways Authority Ordinance, 2001.
(2) It extends to the whole of
the North‑West Frontier Province.
(3) It shall come into force at
once, and shall always be deemed to have taken effect on 1st July, 2001.

dated 29‑8‑2001.‑‑The following Ordinance by the
Governor of the North‑West Frontier Province is hereby published for

CHAPTER ‑ I
PRELIMINARY
2. Definitions.‑‑
In this Ordinance, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or
context,‑‑
(a)
"Auditor General" means the Auditor General of Pakistan;
(b)
"Authority" means the Frontier Highways Authority established under
section 3;
(c)
"Board" means the Executive Board of the Authority;
(d)
"Council" means the Frontier Highways Council;
(e)
"Provincial Highway", for the purposes of this Ordinance, shall mean,
a road declared by Government,
by Notification in the Official Gazette under section 10, to be a Provincial Highway;
(f)
"Government" means the Government of the North-West Frontier
Province;
(g)
"Managing Director" means the Managing Director of the Authority;
(h)
"member" means a member of the Council or, as the case may be, of the
Board;
(i)
"President" means the President of the Council;
(j)
"regulations" means regulations framed under this Ordinance;
(k)
"right of way (ROW)" means the land acquired for the purpose of
construction of a Highway or any
other road assigned to the Authority, or area astride a highway, the limits of which shall be notified, within which the
control of land use shall rest
with the Authority;
(l)
"road" means a road including land within the right of way and all
works, such as carriageways,
cartways, footpaths, berms, side drains, culverts, bridges, tunnels, fences, posts, sign boards,
plantation and lighting arrangements, intersections
and medians plantation assigned to the Authority; and
(m)
"rules" means rules made under this Ordinance.

[Gazette of

No. Legis: 1‑(15)/71,
dated 29‑8‑2001.‑‑The following Ordinance by the
Governor of the North‑West Frontier Province is hereby published for
general information:‑‑
CHAPTER‑II
ESTABLISHMENT AND MANAGEMENT OF THE AUTHORITY
3. Establishment of Frontier
Highways Authority.‑‑(1) As from the commencement of this
Ordinance, there shall be established, for carrying out the purposes of this
Ordinance, an Authority to be known as the Frontier Highways Authority.
(2) The Authority shall be a body
corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal with power to acquire,
hold and dispose of property, and may by its name sue and be sued.
(3) The Headquarters of the
Authority shall be at Peshawar.
(4) The power of general
direction and administration of the Authority and its affairs shall vest in the
Frontier Highways Council, which may, through Board, exercise all powers and do all acts and things, which may
be exercised or done by the Authority in accordance with the provisions of this
Ordinance.
(5) The Authority, or for that
matter the Frontier Highways Council, shall work under the general
superintendence and control of Government in the Works and Services Department.

the Authority.‑‑The purpose and functions of the Authority
shall be to plan, promote, organize and implement programmes for construction,
development, operations, repairs and maintenance of Provincial Highways and
other roads specially entrusted to it by Government.

CHAPTER‑II

7. Management.‑‑(1)
The powers for the Management of the Authority and its affairs shall be
exercised by the Board;
(2) The Board shall consist of a
Chairman, who shall be the Managing Director, and not more than three members
to be appointed by the Frontier Highways Council as under:
(i)
a representative of the Finance Department of the rank of an Additional Secretary or equivalent;
(ii)
a representative of the Works and Services Department; and
(iii)
an officer of the Authority from the field of Engineering in BPS‑20, to
be nominated by the Council.
(3) The meetings of the Board
shall be held at the Head Office of the Frontier Highways Authority after every
three months or at any time before three months if so desired by the Chairman
of the Board.
(4) The Chairman or, in his absence,
a member authorized by him on his behalf, and three members shall constitute a
'quorum' for a meeting of the Board.

CHAPTER‑II

9. Managing Director, his
duties, functions and powers.‑‑(1) The Governor of the North‑West
Frontier Province shall appoint the Managing Director who shall be the Chief
Executive of the Authority and Chairman of the Board and shall exercise such
powers and perform such functions as may be specified by the Council.
(2) The Managing Director shall
receive such salary and allowances and be subject to such conditions of service
as may be determined by the Council.
(3) The Managing Director shall
have the power to re‑appropriate with the approval of the Board, and the
amount, including the re -appropriated amount, shall remain within the limit of
approval cost and must not exceed the permissible excess.

The powers of the Authority

NORTH﷓WEST FRONTIER PROVINCE HIGHWAYS AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 2001

FRONTIER PROVINCE HIGHWAYS AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 2001
ORDINANCE XIX OF 2001
An Ordinance

Frontier Province
[Gazette of
N.W.F.P., Extraordinary, 29th August, 2001]
No. Legis: 1‑(15)/71,
dated 29‑8‑2001.‑‑The following Ordinance by the
Governor of the North‑West Frontier Province is hereby published for
general information:‑‑
CHAPTER‑III
POWERS AND DUTIES OF THE AUTHORITY
10. The powers of the
Authority.‑‑(1) The Authority may take such measures and
exercise such powers, as it considers necessary or expedient for carrying out
the purposes of this Ordinance.
(2) Without prejudice to the
generality of the powers conferred by subsection (1), the Authority may, for
carrying out the purposes of this Ordinance,‑‑
(i)
prepare and notify in the official Gazette, a list of Provincial Highways duly approved by the Cabinet and Government;
(ii)
advise Government on matters relating to Provincial Highways and other roads;
(iii)
acquire any land in accordance with legal procedure and obtain and dispose of movable and immovable property or
interests therein;
(iv)
undertake any work specified in subsections (1) and (2) of section 11;
(v)
incur expenditure on works specified in clause (iii);
(vi)
procure plant, machinery, instruments and materials required for its use;
(vii)
enter into and perform all such contracts as it may consider necessary;
(viii)
levy, collect or cause to be collected tolls on Frontier Highways and such other roads as may be entrusted to it and
bridges thereon;
(ix)
licence facilities on roads under its control an such terms as it deems fit;
(x)
notify the right of way within which it shall not be lawful, without the
consent of the Authority, to
make any changes in the land use;
(xi)
cause studies, surveys, experiments and technical research to be made or contribute towards the cost of such studies,
surveys, experiments or technical researches
made by any other agency;
(xii)
exercise power to award negotiated contracts for projects to be undertaken through Private Sector Financing
Programmes;
(xiii)
seek and obtain advice and assistance from any agency for the preparation and execution of any plan, programme
or project;
(xiv)
raise funds (local and foreign) through, borrowing, floating of bonds, sharing or leasing of assets or any
other means, from time to time with approval of
Government:
Provided that a foreign loan
shall be negotiated in consultation with the relevant Ministry of Government of
Pakistan besides the Finance Department of Government;
(xv)
perform any other function supplemental, incidental or consequential to the purposes and functions aforesaid; and
(xvi)
undertake mutation of land as soon as the land is taken over.

CHAPTER‑III
POWERS AND DUTIES OF THE AUTHORITY
11. Plans and Schemes.‑‑(1)
The authority shall prepare a master plan for the development, construction,
operation and maintenance of Frontier Highways and roads in the North‑West
Frontier Province for the approval of the Council.
(2) The Authority may frame a
scheme or schemes for all or any of the following matters, namely:
(i)
construction, remodelling; operation and development of Provincial Highways and other roads entrusted to it by
Government;
(ii)
research and development in the field of Highways;
(iii)
training of the Authority's employees;
(vi)
welfare of the Authority's employees; and
(v)
any other matter pertaining to the purposes and functions of the Authority or incidental thereto.

CHAPTER‑III

12. Powers to eject
unauthorized occupants.‑‑Subject to rules, the authority shall
have the power to summarily eject any unauthorized occupant of Provincial
Highways or other road entrusted to it or proposed site thereof or within the
limits where raising of structures is prohibited and demolish and remove any
structure thereon, and to use such force, including police force, as may be
necessary for the purpose and to recover the cost thereof from the person
responsible for such occupation or obstruction.

13. Appointment of officers,
servants etc.‑‑(1) The Authority may from time to time employ
on contract basis such officers and servants, or appoint such experts or
consultants, as it may consider necessary for the performance of its functions,
on such terms and conditions as it may deem fit.
(2) Notwithstanding anything
contained in subsection (1), any rule made, or order or instruction issued, by
the Authority, or in the terms and conditions of service of any person employed
by or serving under the Authority, the Authority may at any time terminate the
services of any person, as may be prescribed.
(3) The officers and servants of
the Works and Services Department transferred to serve under the Authority
shall be deemed to be on deputation, without payment of deputation allowance,
but shall be entitled to the salary, allowances and other service benefits as
admissible to them as civil servants.

reports and returns, etc.‑‑(1) The Authority shall submit to
Government, as soon as possible after the end of every financial year but
before the last day of September next following, report on the conduct of its
affairs for that year.
(2) A copy of the report
mentioned in subsection (1), together with a copy of the audit report shall be
placed by Government before the Provincial Assembly and the Provincial Assembly
shall refer the same to its Committee on Public Accounts for scrutiny and
examination.
(3) The Committee on Public
Accounts shall scrutinize and examine the reports referred to it under
subsection (2) in the same manner as, and shall in respect thereof, perform the
same functions and exercise the same powers, as are required by it to be
performed and exercised in respect of appropriation of accounts of the
Provincial Government and the report of the General thereon.
(4) The Provincial Government may
ask the Authority to furnish it with‑‑
(i)
any return, statement, estimate, statistics or other information regarding any matter under the control of the Authority; or
(ii)
a report on any such matter; or
(iii)
a copy of any document in the charge of the Authority; and the Authority shall comply with all such requisitions.

sections.description:
Frontier Highways Authority Fund and Budget

NORTH﷓WEST FRONTIER PROVINCE HIGHWAYS AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 2001
NORTH‑WEST
FRONTIER PROVINCE HIGHWAYS AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 2001
ORDINANCE XIX OF 2001
An Ordinance
further to provide for establishment of a Highway Authority to the North‑West
Frontier Province
[Gazette of
N.W.F.P., Extraordinary, 29th August, 2001]
No. Legis: 1‑(15)/71,
dated 29‑8‑2001.‑‑The following Ordinance by the
Governor of the North‑West Frontier Province is hereby published for
general information:‑‑
CHAPTER‑VI
FINANCE
21. Frontier Highways
Authority Fund and Budget.‑‑There shall be formed a non‑lapsable
fund vesting in the Authority known as the "Frontier Highways Authority
Fund", to be utilized by the Authority to meet charges in connection with
its functions under this Ordinance including remuneration to its employees.
(2) The Provincial Highways
Authority Fund shall be kept in scheduled banks and shall be operated according
to rules and regulations of the Authority.
(3) The Frontier Highways
Authority Fund shall have to its credit all funds received by the Authority
from which the Authority can incur expenditure related to its functions
including‑‑‑
(i)
loans obtained from the Government, including the Federal Government;
(ii)
other loans obtained by the Authority;
(iii)
grants made or funds provided by the Government and the Federal Government;
(iv)
income from tolls;
(v)
foreign aid, grants and loans negotiated and raised by the Authority with the approval of Government;
(vi)
all other sums received by the Authority, such as fees, damages costs, refunds, forfeitures, sale proceeds,
lease money, rentals and fines;
(vii)
income from the sale of assets, land or vehicles belonging to the Authority;
(viii)
funds from floating bonds, shares or through any other means, if so permitted by Government; and
(ix)
the following provincial receipts, which heretofore form part of Provincial Consolidated Fund, shall henceforth
be credited to the Frontier Highways Authority
Fund.
(4) The budget of the Authority
shall be maintained under two separate heads, firstly "Construction/Development
Budget" and secondly "Repair, Maintenance and Operation Budget";
provided that any re‑appropriation between the two heads shall require
approval of the Cabinet and Government.
(5) The following shall be
credited to the Frontier Highways Authority Fund:
(a)
renewal of fee of contractor's registrations;
(b)
stamp duty on execution of contract agreements;
(c)
sale of tender forms;
(d)
initial fee of CNG/Petrol Pumps on Frontier Highways;
(e)
lease of approaches to service stations/CNG Petrol Pumps on/from Frontier Highways; and
(f)
toll‑tax on Frontier Highways.

No. Legis: 1‑(15)/71,
dated 29‑8‑2001.‑‑The following Ordinance by the
Governor of the North‑West Frontier Province is hereby published for
general information:‑‑
CHAPTER‑VII
MISCELLANEOUS
29. Power to enter.‑‑Subject
to any regulation made in this behalf, any person generally or specially
authorized by the Authority may, whenever it is necessary for the purposes of
this Ordinance at all reasonable times, enter upon any land or premises, for
the purposes stated hereunder without causing any damages to the private or
public property:
(i)
making any inspection survey, measurement, valuation or inquiry;
(ii)
taking levels;
(iii)
digging or bore into sub‑soil;
(iv)
setting out boundaries and intended lines of work;
(v)
marking such levels, boundaries and lines by placing marks and cutting trenches; and
(vi)
doing such other acts or things as may be prescribed:
Provided that no such person
shall enter any boundary or any enclosed court or garden attached to a dwelling‑house,
except with the consent of the occupant thereof after serving on him at least
twenty‑four hours notice in writing of his intention to do so.
